scenes.headline: How a 200 GB MoE decodes on one 3090
scenes.sub: Experts in system RAM, a cache in VRAM, the CPU on the misses.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Vada! Today: how a huge mixture of experts model runs on one gaming card, with its experts in system memory.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Decode reads only the experts each token routes to, so they can live in RAM; who computes the misses sets the speed.
scenes.say: Each token reads only the experts its router picks. So experts can live in system memory. What matters is who computes the misses.

steps.say: Attention, the router and the shared expert stay on the card, because every token reads them.
Six experts are picked per layer. The hottest sit in a cache in video memory.
The rest miss. Their home copy is pinned in eight channels of DDR4.
Twenty-two CPU cores compute the misses in place, and return a small partial sum.

scenes.title: The ceiling
scenes.text: tok/s = bandwidth / routed bytes per token
scenes.say: The speed limit is one division.

parts.say: One DeepSeek token reads about three gigabytes of experts.
Eight DDR4 channels would allow about sixty-four tokens a second.

scenes.title: Per layer: PCIe or CPU?
scenes.say: Each layer holds a small auction.

items.text: Try k misses on the CPU

items.say: Send the rest across the slot.

scenes.title: Decode, one stream, tok/s
scenes.note: Speeds measured by the repo; the ceiling is reasoned
scenes.say: Streaming misses over the slot gave four tokens a second. The CPU tier and cache gave twenty-one, under a ceiling near twenty-eight.

left.title: If RAM set the pace
left.say: If memory were the limit, misses would cost about nine milliseconds a token.

right.title: What the code budgets
right.say: The code budgets three times that. Decoding a codebook quant is arithmetic, and the cores run out first.

steps.say: The second post: Strata on one 3090 with DDR5, decoding Qwen near ninety-seven tokens a second.
Its author saw little change between DDR4 and DDR5. Same story.

scenes.text: Routed bytes per token decide whether it runs; the CPU's arithmetic, not the RAM bus, decides how fast.

recap: A VRAM cache serves 41% of reads
CPU arithmetic, not DDR4, is the limit
scenes.say: Read only what you route to, cache the hot experts, and mind the CPU's arithmetic.
